title: DDoS Spam Attack Solana ACM CCS 2024
text:
DDoS and Spam Attacks on Solana - ACM CCS 2024

Attack patterns identified:
- Low-fee transaction flooding overwhelms leader TPU
- Spam bursts of 100k+ TPS degrade network to <1k real TPS  
- QUIC stream exhaustion blocks legitimate clients
- Vote transaction spam disrupts consensus timing
- Failed transaction spam wastes validator compute

Technical details:
- Solana processes transactions via QUIC protocol on TPU port
- Attackers open max QUIC streams without sending valid transactions
- UDP-based gossip susceptible to amplification attacks
- Leader rotation predictable 4 slots ahead - enables targeted attacks

Impact observed:
- September 2021: NFT mint caused 17-hour outage
- April 2022: NFT bot spam caused network halt
- June 2022: Concentrated spam caused validator restart
- Network degraded to <100 TPS during attacks

Mitigations:
- Stake-weighted QoS: validators prioritize high-stake transaction senders
- Priority fees: economic cost to spam
- QUIC connection limits per IP
- Local fee markets per compute unit
- Jito Solana client modifications for spam filtering
Source: ACM CCS 2024
